headline: Large Energy User Cost Shift
short_summary: This bill aims to shift the financial burden of grid infrastructure costs from residential ratepayers to large energy users, primarily data centers.
status: Last Action: Governor's Action Deadline 11:59 p.m., May 23, 2026 on 2026-04-22
supporters: Del. Destiny LeVere Bolling, Sen. Louise Lucas, Dominion Energy (initially), low-income customers.
opponents: Data Center Coalition (concerned about language precluding analysis of capacity costs), Governor Spanberger (amendments seen as weakening).
news_headline: Virginia governor amends bills that shift costs onto data centers
news_summary: Governor Spanberger proposed amendments to HB 1393 and SB 253, which aimed to shift energy costs onto data centers to save residential customers money and expand a power line burial program. Critics argue the governor's changes weaken the original intent of the bills, particularly by removing the direct shift of capacity auction costs and instead allowing the SCC to determine fair share.

headline: Data Center Water Use Reporting
short_summary: This bill mandates water users providing water to data centers to report their total monthly water consumption, including reclaimed water, to the State Water Control Board.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Sen. Kannan Srinivasan, Del. Liz Guzman, environmental advocates, concerned constituents.
opponents: Not explicitly mentioned in search results.
news_headline: Four data center bills await governor's signature in Virginia
news_summary: SB 553, one of four bills on the governor's desk, aims to increase reporting requirements for data center water usage, bringing transparency to their water consumption. Supporters view it as a necessary check and balance for the rapidly growing data center industry.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise
short_summary: This bill requires applicants for new high energy use facilities, such as data centers, to submit a site assessment focusing on noise impacts before local approval, while preserving local zoning authority.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Del. Joshua Thomas, Del. Elizabeth Guzman, concerned constituents, local communities.
opponents: Not explicitly mentioned, but data center developers may find new siting requirements challenging.
news_headline: Loudoun Co. officials discuss data center noise mitigation efforts
news_summary: Growing concerns about noise from data centers, particularly in Loudoun County, are prompting officials to discuss mitigation efforts and potential changes to zoning ordinances. Residents report constant hums and high-frequency ringing, highlighting the clash between data center growth and community quality of life.
